newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices catch up on U.S. rise.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices catch up on U.S. rise.

text.p: Danish bond prices moved up on Friday in a delayed reaction to a rise in U.S. treasuries that came too late on Thursday to stop Danish paper slipping.
"Thursday's American consumer price data for July was well received but the first serious reaction only came as the Danish market closed," a dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 opened at 112.62, yielding 6.05 percent, up 0.14 point from Thursday.
The seven percent 2007 paper, the benchmark from September 1, was up 0.10 point to 105.50, yielding 6.25 percent. Its yield spread to the German bund widened one basis point to 61 bp.
The crown firmed slightly, to 3.8090 to the mark from Thursday's 3.8093.
U.S. strength supports the long end of the Danish market, while the short end is still affected by uncertainty over German interest rates and the terms of coming monetary union.

While the two to 10-year Danish spread was expected to flatten on Friday the Danish-German 10-year spread was expected to be around the 60 basis point level and to not stray far until publication on August 26 of the government's 1998 budget proposals --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33-969650
